title: Resident Coinsurance Charge for a Booked Block: How the Amount Is Computed (Medicare Part A Skilled Nursing Facility Coverage)
content:
**Medicare Part A Skilled Nursing Facility Coverage — the resident coinsurance charge.** The resident coinsurance charge for a block prices one booked coinsurance block: among the coverage's booked-days entries in the band of benefit days 21 through 100, the one whose last service date is the latest.

**Record test.** The resident coinsurance charge is worked out only for a charged block that passes this record test: its service month carries one booked-days entry in the band of benefit days 21 through 100; at most one such entry of the coverage has the last benefit day just before the charged block's first benefit day; the bed-hold records book at most one leave for its service month and take back none of that leave's held days; its booked-days entry carries at most one day reversal for each reason and none for a booking error; no hospital-day or leave-of-absence reversal on it covers a held night of that leave, and each such reversal counts every day of its span; an uncertified-day reversal on it counts every day of its span except the held nights and the hospital-day and leave-of-absence days inside the span; and, when the supplemental effective date falls after the charged block's first service date, the block before it either has a resident charge billing exactly 100, 50 or 25 percent of that charge's own days times its own daily rate, to within half a percentage point, or carries a secondary charge and no resident charge; and, when the resident's charge for the charged block stands, its day count equals the charged block's booked days less the days of every day reversal posted against its booked-days entry on or before the date that charge was posted; and the charged block's last service date falls in 2024 or later. The block before the charged block is the coverage's booked-days entry in the band of benefit days 21 through 100 whose last benefit day is the day before the charged block's first benefit day; its resident charge is the resident coinsurance charge posted for it that is not a rebill of a denied secondary share.

**Days before the supplemental effective date.** For a block that passes its record test, the resident coinsurance charge, the card payment, the rate-year correction, the reduction for reversed covered days and the bank draft each count the days before the supplemental effective date as their own policies state, and only for such a block; for every other block, the tier that sets the split is the one in effect on the days of service: a Medigap policy changes the split from the carrier's policy effective date and QMB protection from the first day of the month after the state's QMB determination, so days before the supplemental effective date keep the earlier split, and none of these five figures is priced for it.

**The figure.**

1. The resident coinsurance charge prices each day it counts at the daily coinsurance rate of 217.00, and days before the supplemental effective date take the earlier share of 100 percent.
2. The supplemental effective date the resident coinsurance charge reads is the one recorded on the coverage; a coverage that records none has the tier on file in effect on every day of the charged block.
3. The resident coinsurance charge counts the charged block's covered days, which are its booked days less every day reversed against its booked-days entry.
4. The days the resident coinsurance charge counts before the supplemental effective date are first its calendar days of the charged block before that date: when the date falls after the charged block's first service date and on or before its last, the days from the first service date up to the day before the date; when it falls after the last service date, every calendar day of the charged block; otherwise none.
5. Each kind of day named below that is not a covered day is taken off those days, never leaving fewer than none nor more than the days the resident coinsurance charge counts.
6. A day reversed as a leave-of-absence day is not a covered day: when the charged block's booked-days entry carries a leave-of-absence reversal, its reversed days inside the charged block come off the days the resident coinsurance charge counts before the supplemental effective date, all of them when its last reversed day falls before that date, those from its first reversed day up to the day before the date when the date falls after its first reversed day and on or before its last, and none otherwise; without such a reversal, none come off.
7. Days the resident coinsurance charge counts before the supplemental effective date take the earlier share; every other day it counts takes the resident share of the tier on file. The resident share of the tier on file is that tier's resident share percent in the cost-sharing split schedule. When the tier on file prohibits balance billing, as the QMB Medicaid Crossover tier does, the resident coinsurance charge bills the resident nothing for any day on or after the tier's supplemental effective date, those days taking the tier's resident share of nothing, while days before that date keep the earlier split, QMB protection not reaching back before it.
8. The resident coinsurance charge adds, over the days it counts, the daily rate times the share each day takes, divides the sum by 100 and rounds it half up to the cent once.

### Hypothetical worked examples

A coverage held in the tier without supplemental coverage until the state's QMB determination in April 2026 now sits in the QMB Medicaid Crossover tier (resident share 0 percent), with 1 May 2026 recorded as its supplemental effective date. The March 2026 block before carries a resident charge billing 100 percent of its own days times its own daily rate.

*Example 1 — the April 2026 block.* The charged block runs from 1 April to 30 April: 30 booked days. Its booked-days entry carries a leave-of-absence reversal of 14 and 15 April (2 days). The block passes its record test.
- Covered days: 30 less 2, that is 28.
- The supplemental effective date falls after the last service date, so every calendar day of the block, 30, comes first; less the 2 leave-of-absence days, 28 days take the earlier share of 100 percent.
- No day falls on or after the date.
- Sum of daily rate times share: 217.00 times 28 times 100, that is 607600; divided by 100 and rounded half up to the cent once: **6076.00**.

*Example 2 — the May 2026 block.* The charged block runs from 1 May to 19 May: 19 booked days, none reversed. The supplemental effective date does not fall after the first service date, so no day comes before it; all 19 days take the QMB tier's resident share of nothing, and the resident coinsurance charge is **0.00**.
